clips.caption:
1971, Stanford: ordinary students, peace signs and all, split at random into guards and inmates for what was supposed to be a two-week study.

It didn't make two weeks. Within days the guards turned cruel and the inmates started breaking down — people who knew each other, who'd spent the whole summer together, turned on one another once one side held power over the other. Nobody's personality changed. The power did. Give almost anyone enough of it with no one watching, and the same thing happens.
